title: best ai to vibe code with no limits
author: unknow67172571
selftext: i want to find an ai to help me create me a lil fun game to play. I got all of the assets i just need a coding ai to just get me some codes

comments.author: Alternative_Sink9000
comments.body: no limit is a no go. Your best bet is something like Direct API DeepSeek. But then again, I think you get more DeepSeek out of opencode $10 subs compared to direct api.

replies.author: orellanaed
replies.body: Claude plan + Flockbay (Godot) is my go-to

comments.author: RichardTheApe
comments.body:
If you don’t want to use the credit system you’ll have to go open source or API though API as you’ll find out is still pretty expensive. If you want no limit your only option is to self host but that’s just doing away with monthly subscription to pay a high upfront cost and ongoing electricity/maintenance as well as any labor you have to put in up front to get it working and on going to keep it working. 

Overall I actually think for 20 bucks you get what you need from Claude for most user. That said I think if you’re serious about the work and have the capital check out Qwen and research self hosting

comments.author: Slow-Win8148
comments.body: There is nothing such as no limits, there used to be plans like this but with stronger models the inference cost can't sustain limitless usage. You can use cheap models like deepseek 4.1 flash or mimo 2.6 flash but tbh they suck at game dev.

comments.author: HistoricalEngineer74
comments.body: You'll get far with the $20 pro plan from claude when doing it for fun.

comments.author: Lexroid_1
comments.body:
If you want no limits you have to go with local ai models, which requiers a powerfull rig to run. for me I have always used claude for coding. for my work, pro subscription is good enough. I do not like to use gpt, it talkes to much. but that is a personal prefrence. I have used them both at the same time, both on claude on pro and gpt on pluse. used a skill called delegate skill, it is good if you want to split the work and have both work on the project. it saves tokens. but again that is my personl prefrence. 

here is the skill if any one is interested (was not made by me): 

https://github.com/amElnagdy/delegate-skills

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body: AI coding requires real money to run, so if you have limited money, use cheap models and ask them to do write simple code, using existing libraries.

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body:
There's no such thing as "no limit" AI. Compute costs money. 

You either buy a computer or you pay for compute.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body: A local model on your own hardware. Literally everything else will have limits unless your budget isn't limited.

comments.author: raviteja777
comments.body: If you have a good enuf PC with say atleast 24GB or more graphic card , you can host free or open sourced models using LMStudio or Ollama, then you can use plugins like continue.dev or cline to run coding agents .... but still they wont match the level of online paid ones.

comments.author: nexuscoregaming
comments.body: Closest thing are open weights, but even then you need: 1. A lot of computing power. 2. Training for your specific purpose. 3. Pay for the electricity used lol. So basically what you're asking for is a unicorn.

comments.author: MaqeSweden
comments.body:
Opencode lets you use Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 for free right now.

Not the best, but definitely enough to create your first fun little game. Not as smart as claude or codex, so you'll need to guide it in smaller iterations but it can be done.

Not that much worse than Gemini.

comments.author: Bulky_Blood_7362
comments.body:
Use qwen 3.8 flash next locally.

It's the best model you can run locally for free with a high-end gaming pc.

Other then that... there's no free, maybe through free chat llms but you're not going to get far

comments.author: Seerix
comments.body:
$20 to claude will be enough to get a prototype going and if you really get into it, the $100 is pretty great right now. Use Opus 5.5 in claude code or whatever their app is called. Cowork? I dunno.

Currently the best sub deal on offer imo. You could try chinese models but if you don't really know much about coding you tend to need to guide them a lot more than Claude or ChatGPT
